page: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with 8 dedicated Intel x86_64 vCPUs, consisting of 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, running at a base speed of 2.0 GHz. The system features 40.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 5.0 GB per core. For accelerated workloads, it includes a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with a 0.3333 allocation, delivering 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 740 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show average performance across general compute and memory tasks, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 14,175.12 and a PassMark CPU score of 14,090.9. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 88.57 GB/sec for read operations and 52.63 GB/sec for write operations. However, the server excels in GPU-driven tasks; LLM inference benchmarks for a medium 7B model show top-tier performance, achieving 3,147.67 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 107.73 tokens/sec for text generation.

By utilizing a fractional GPU slice rather than a full dedicated card, this server type offers a cost-effective resource profile for workloads that require GPU acceleration but do not scale to a full A40 footprint. The combination of 16 GB VRAM, 40.0 GB of system memory, and fast NVMe storage makes this instance highly suitable for small to medium LLM inference, machine learning model development, database operations, and GPU-accelerated data processing.
